TO THE ABOVE-NAMED DEFENDANT(S):

You are hereby summoned to answer the complaint in this action, and to serve a copy of
your answer, or, if the complaint is not served with this summons, to serve a notice of appearance on
the Plaintiff's attorney(s) within twenty days after the service of this summons, exclusive of the day of
service, where service is made by delivery upon you personally within the state, or, within 30 days after
completion of service where service is made in any other manner. In case of your failure to appear or
answer, judgment will be taken against you by default for the relief demanded in the complaint.

Plaintiff designates New York County as the place of trial. The basis of venue is pursuant to
the CPLR 505(a), which provides that “[t]he place of trial of an action by or against a public authority
constituted under the laws of the state shall be in the county in which the authority has its principal
office or where it has facilities involved in the action.”

Plaintiff, Justin Sapini, by and through his attorneys, STOLZENBERGCORTELLI, LLP,
complaining of the defendants, Anthony F. Ferrara (hereinafter, “Ferrara”) and Metro-North
Commuter Railroad (hereinafter, “Metro-North”), respectfully alleges as follows:

NTROD ION
1 On April 23, 2023, Plaintiff Justin Sapini, while operating his motor vehicle, was involved in a
collision with a vehicle operated by Defendant Anthony F. Ferrara, who, upon information and belief,
is an employee of Metro-North and that the vehicle that Ferrara was Operating was owned and
maintained by Metro-North. The collision occurred in Westchester County. Plaintiff suffered a
“serious injury” as a result of the collision. Defendants, therefore, are liable to Plaintiff for their
negligence. This matter, previously dismissed, is renewed pursuant to CPLR 205.

THE PARTIES

2. Plaintiff was formerly a resident of 7 Valley Drive, Nanuet, County of Rockland and State of

New York.
3. He is now a resident of Texas.
4, Upon information and belief, at all times hereinafter mentioned, MT'A was and still is a public

authority and existing under and by virtue of the laws of the State of New York.
5. MTA’s principal office is located in New York County.

THE COLLISION
25. That at all times herein mentioned, on April 23, 2023, at approximately 8:30 a.m., Plaintiff was
the operator of a certain 2012 Volkswagen motor vehicle bearing New York State license plate number
KYR1393 for the year 2023.
26. That at all times hereinafter mentioned, on April 23, 2023, Cedar Street at or near its
intersection with Garden Street, City of New Rochelle, County of Westchester and State of New York,
was and still is a public thoroughfare.
27. That at all times hereinafter mentioned, on April 23, 2023, at approximately 8:30 a.m., Ferrara
operated Defendants’ vehicle on Cedar Street at or near the intersection of Garden Street, City of
New Rochelle, County of Westchester and State of New York. Ferrara was in the course of his
employment, pulling into a Metro-North facility, when the collision occurred.
28. That at all times hereinafter mentioned, on April 23, 2023, at approximately 8:30 a.m., Plaintiff
operated the his vehicle on Cedar Street at or near the intersection of Garden Street, City of New
Rochelle, County of Westchester and State of New York,
29. That on April 23, 2023, at approximately 8:30 a.m., at the aforementioned location,
immediately adjacent to a Metro-North facility, the Defendants’ vehicle came into contact with the

motor vehicle owned and operated by Plaintiff (“the Collison”).

30. That as a result of the aforesaid collision, Plaintiff was seriously injured.
FEND. E I
Ff. That the aforesaid occurrence was caused wholly and solely by reason of the negligence of the

Defendants without any fault or negligence on the part of the Plaintiff contributing thereto.
32. That the serious and severe personal injuries sustained by the Plaintiff were occasioned solely
and wholly through and by reason of the carelessness, recklessness and negligence of the defendants

in the ownership, operation, management, maintenance and control of the within motor vehicle; in

operating same without due regard to the rights and safety of the plaintiff; in failing to properly steer,
guide, manage and control said motor vehicle; in carelessly and negligently merging into plaintiffs lane
of travel without ensuring it was safe to do so; in carelessly and negligently operating the said motor
vehicle over and along a public highway at a high and/or excessive rate of speed and/or at a greater
tate of speed than care and caution would permit under the circumstances and conditions then and
there existing to the knowledge of the defendants; in failing to maintain a safe and adequate distance
from plaintiff's vehicle; in failing to apply the brakes or slow down or stop in such a manner as would
have prevented the occurrence; in failing to make adequate and timely observation of and response to
conditions; in failing to keep a proper look-out when controlling said motor vehicle; in carelessly and
negligently disregarding traffic control devices in place at the scene of the occurrence then and there
in effect; in failing to see plaintiffs vehicle; in driving into plaintiffs vehicle; in driving into traffic
without ensuring that it was safe to do so; in operating said motor vehicle in violation of the traffic
tules, regulations, statutes and ordinances; in failing to avoid a collision with the plaintiff; and the
defendant, ANTHONY F. FERRARA, was otherwise careless and negligent in failing and omitting
to take proper and suitable precautions to avoid the said occurrence. Defendant, METRO-NORTH
COMMUTER RAILROAD, was further careless and reckless in the negligent entrustment of said
motor vehicle to defendant, ANTHONY F, FERRARA.

33. In the alternative, Defendant Anthony Ferrara was not working at the time of this collision,
but was on a break and thus this accident did not occur during the scope of his employment.

INJURIES

34. That by reason of the foregoing, Plaintiff sustained severe and permanent personal injuries,
became sick, sore, lame and disabled; suffered injuries to his nervous system; suffered mental anguish,

was confined to hospital, bed and home and may, in the future, be so confined; was incapacitated

adding Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA), and making the same allegations. See Summns & Complnt., Sapini
v. MTA (Index No. 150940/ 2024), ECF 1. Then, on multiple occasions, including February 20, 2024 and March 14, 2024,
Plaintiff communicated with defendants, seeking to provide updates regarding the claims, and supplying medical records.
Among this information, we provided a document we entitled “Presentation of Claim,” which considered multiple records
relevant to Plaintiff's liability and damages claims. See Ltr (dated 3/14/24), Sapini v. MTA (Index No. 150940/2024), ECF
22. Plaintiff learned after commencement of suit that MTA was not a proper party as it was advised that Ferrara was an
employee of Metro-North. Then, on April 8, 2024, Plaintiff cross-moved for leave to amend the Complaint to (1) remove
MTA from the caption and (2) add compliance with the Public Authorities Law. See Notice of Cross Mot (ECF 13). It
should be noted that Public Authorities Law § 1276(1) provides that as a condition to an action against Metro-North for
